title: Tenant-configurable priority lanes for latency-sensitive streaming + tool-calls intake
creator: Lena Sørensen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are asking for self-serve controls to route streaming chat + multi-action tool-calls into priority lanes that honor tenant SLAs (latency SLOs, cost budget, and data residency). Current intake is manual — PMs triage requests and ask infra/ops to create custom routing rules. This creates delays, inconsistent prioritization, and frequent operational support.

Goal: Build a tenant-facing Priority Lane Configurator (UI + API) that lets tenant admins define rules for live routing of inbound hosted-API requests into prioritized execution lanes (e.g., 'low-latency', 'economic', 'fallback'), with clear opt-in guardrails, audit logs, and automatic fallbacks for capacity/region failures. The feature should integrate with existing rollout policies and Redwood's model-variant fallback logic. Scope includes product UX, schema for rule definitions, backend routing policy extension, rollout/canary support, observability hooks for cost/latency, and documentation.

Out of scope: Re-writing core kernel scheduling or baking new quantization algorithms — changes should use existing runtime capabilities and routing primitives where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant admin UI: create/edit/delete priority lane rules with conditions (tenant, route, model tag, request class, estimated token size, geo) and target lane (low-latency/economic/fallback)
API: programmatic Rule CRUD endpoints matching UI schema with RBAC checks and KMS-logged changes
Runtime: requests that match a tenant rule are routed to the configured execution lane and respect lane-specific quotas and autoscale profiles
Fallbacks: when target lane is unavailable, requests failover to configured compatible lanes per rule with transparent headers for tracing
Observability: dashboard surface with per-lane latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, and a timeline of rule changes; alerts if rule causes >=10% latency regression vs baseline
Audit: every rule change emits an auditable event (who/what/when) and is retained per tenant retention policy
Migration: existing manual escalations and custom routing jobs are importable via CSV or admin-assist flow
notes: Design and engineering collaboration required: early wireframes to validate complexity of rule predicates. Prioritize predicates that map directly to runtime signals to avoid large infra work (e.g., model-tag, route, tenant-tier, region). Consider a 'preview' mode that simulates routing for a 24-hour sample window before activation. Trade-offs: finer-grained predicates increase power but also complexity and support burden. Detect and block predicates that could bypass compliance (e.g., cross-region rules that violate customer VPC constraints).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag toggled per-tenant; 2) Beta with 3 customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market SaaS, one regulated tenant) for 4 weeks with dedicated telemetry; 3) Open to self-serve for paid tiers after no critical regressions; 4) Post-launch 2-week hypercare with engineering on-call
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfigured rules could route high-volume traffic into small capacity pools -> mitigation: default soft-quotas and pre-activation simulation
Risk: Rules that violate data residency -> mitigation: validation layer that enforces tenant region constraints, block on creation
Risk: Increased support cost from complex predicates -> mitigation: limit predicate set for self-serve to 6 vetted signals, advanced predicates via professional services
